rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 41 first promises Muslims political authority, starting with the land of God’s House as the community’s heart; Muslims must fulfill the same obligations wherever granted authority, or their rule there is illegitimate.
rows.anchor: his verse forms the first glad tidings of political authority of Muslims in this world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer and zakāh are the binding pillars of the sharīʿah, so mentioning them stands for the whole sharīʿah.
rows.anchor: The prayer and the zakāh are the binding forces of the sharī‘ah.

rows.speaker: some simpletons
rows.claim: Some argue that Qur’anic permission to follow maʿrūf lets every group or nation follow its own customary good; the author rejects this reading.
rows.anchor: Some simpletons argue that when the Qur’ ān has allowed people to follow the ma‘rūf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Where God and His messenger have defined right and wrong, people have no discretion; each nation may follow its own maʿrūf only within sharīʿah limits.
rows.anchor: while remaining within the limits of the sharī‘ah, people of every nation can follow their own ma‘rūf.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 41 is a parenthetical explanatory sentence; after it, the discourse that preceded it resumes in the section beginning at verse 42.
rows.anchor: Verse 41 has the status of an explanatory verse that occurs as a parenthetical sentence. The previous discourse now resumes.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The former prophets’ histories and rejecters reassure the Prophet and companions that God’s promises and warnings will all be fulfilled; any delay follows God’s established practice.
rows.anchor: all promises of God are destined to be fulfilled and so are His warnings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s delays test His pious servants and conclusively communicate the truth to His adversaries.
rows.anchor: In this way, God tests His pious servants and conclusively communicates the truth to His adversaries.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s signs and historical remains are visible to attentive observers, but those whose hearts’ eyes are blind remain unmoved.
rows.anchor: those whose hearts’ eyes have gone blind, they cannot be influenced in any way.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must clearly warn adversaries of imminent danger despite disregarding their hostile attitude.
rows.anchor: the Prophet (sws) is also directed to warn his adversaries in a clear way of the imminent danger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic preaching is routinely obstructed, yet God fulfills His word and shames opponents’ plots.
rows.anchor: the word of God was fulfilled and all the mischief worked by their diabolical opponents was put to shame by Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God permits opponents temporary latitude so truth can fully emerge and people of faith and understanding can accept it with insight and remain firm.
rows.anchor: the reason is to make the truth fully blossom and give opportunity to men of faith and understanding

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sense of ‘barren’ extends to harmful or sinister and to a devastating storm with no benefit; the ʿĀd wind and Qamar’s ill-fated day illustrate it.
rows.anchor: From here, the meaning of being harmful and sinister was incorporated in it

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since they await Judgment, they should know all authority will then be God’s; factions, alleged deities, and intercessors cannot help, and God declares victors and vanquished according to deeds, with no chance to earn further reward.
rows.anchor: if these people are only waiting for the Day of Judgment, then they should remember that on the day all authority would rest with God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arrogance in placing themselves above the messengers’ teachings merits punishment in disgrace; humiliation increases punishment’s effect tenfold.
rows.anchor: they regarded themselves to be above and beyond the teachings of God’s messengers which is the worst form of arrogance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Section VI opens by consoling Muslims forced to migrate to preserve faith amid persecution by truth’s enemies, assuring them that God sees and hears all and holds the affair.
rows.anchor: in order to save their faith, were migrating to various regions as a result of the wave of persecution

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As rain revives dead earth, God’s mercy will revive the migrants’ situation and bring them joy.
rows.anchor: Just as a dead piece of earth is revived through rain and becomes brimming with life, in a similar way

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s mercy explains why He is not hasty in punishing enemies, but their respite is limited and failure to value it brings consequences.
rows.anchor: However, His respite has a limit. If they do not duly value it, they will see its fate.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to leave the enemies’ matter to God and ignore their persistent misconduct, since God will soon decide their fate.
rows.anchor: he should consign their matter to God and ignore them. Soon the day will come when God decides their fate.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should tell the idolaters that all their deities together cannot create a fly or recover what it takes from them.
rows.anchor: all their deities combined do not even have the power to create a fly, and cannot even recover a thing a fly snatches away from them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels are God’s servants, not His daughters or partners.
rows.anchor: he angels God’s daughters nor His partners; They are His servants.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God selects envoys from among angels just as He selects them from among human beings.
rows.anchor: From among them, God selects His envoys just as He does so from among human beings.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All are under God’s control; He alone is the fountainhead and decider of every affair.
rows.anchor: They are always under God’s control. It is only He Who is the fountainhead and decider of all affairs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 58 echoes 3:169: those who die for God’s cause are alive and sustained in Barzakh; migrants who die naturally on the way receive the same status as those killed for the cause.
rows.anchor: The same glad tidings are given here to people who migrate from their homes and die on the way though they are not killed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rizq comprehensively includes God’s favors and blessings and should not be restricted; no one can imagine what He will give those who left home and all they had for His cause.
rows.anchor: comprehensively signifies all the favours and blessings of God and should not be confined in its meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of an abode in which migrants are pleased means all their hopes will be fulfilled and much more will be given than they can imagine.
rows.anchor: encompasses a whole world of meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what the migrants endure and, in grace, delays seizing their enemies so they may reform; the respite will end and they will face justice.
rows.anchor: besides being knowledgeable, He is also gracious, He does not immediately seize His enemies.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word dhālika substitutes for an entire sentence.
rows.anchor: is the substitute of a whole sentence, as has been explained under
